title: Readers Prefer Outputs of AI Trained on Copyrighted Books over Expert Human Writers
abstract: arXiv:2510.13939v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The use of copyrighted books for training AI has sparked lawsuits from authors concerned about AI generating derivative content. Yet whether these models can produce high-quality literary text emulating authors' voices remains unclear. We conducted a preregistered study comparing MFA-trained writers with three frontier models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) writing up to 450-word excerpts emulating 50 award-winning authors' styles. In blind pairwise evaluations by 28 MFA-trained readers and 516 college-educated general readers, AI text from in-context prompting was strongly disfavored by MFA readers for stylistic fidelity (OR=0.16) and quality (OR=0.13), while general readers showed no fidelity preference (OR=1.06) but favored AI for quality (OR=1.82). translated_title: 读者更偏爱基于受版权保护书籍训练的AI的输出，而非专家级人类作家
translated_abstract: 将受版权保护的书籍用于训练AI引发了作家的诉讼，他们担心AI会生成衍生内容。然而，这些模型是否能生成模拟作者声音的高质量文学文本仍不清楚。我们进行了一项预注册研究，将受过艺术硕士（MFA）训练的作家与三个前沿模型（ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini）进行比较，让它们撰写模拟50位获奖作家风格的最多450字的文本片段。在由28名MFA训练的读者和516名受过大学教育的普通读者参与的盲测成对评估中，通过上下文提示（in-context prompting）生成的AI文本受到MFA读者的强烈排斥，无论是在风格忠实度（OR=0.16）还是质量（OR=0.13）方面；而普通读者没有表现出忠实度偏好（OR=1.06），但在质量上更偏好AI（OR=1.82）。然而，在作者完整作品上微调ChatGPT后，这些结果发生了逆转：MFA读者更偏好AI的风格忠实度（OR=8.16）和质量（OR=1.87），普通读者则表现出更强的偏好。
tldr: 该研究首次通过大规模盲测评估发现，当前沿AI模型在作者完整作品上微调后，无论是专业文学读者还是普通读者都更偏好AI模拟获奖作家风格的文学输出，超越了人类专家作家，这对版权诉讼中的“替代性作品”争论具有重要启示。
en_tdlr: A preregistered blind evaluation study reveals that fine-tuning frontier AI models on authors' complete works reverses initial reader preferences, making both expert MFA readers and general readers favor AI-generated literary imitations of award-winning authors over expert human writers.
